name: llm-to-jev
title: Replacing an LLM Classifier with Jev
description: Evaluate moving an LLM-based classifier to Jev, which answers with calibrated probabilities instead of text, and carry the move out. Compares Jev with the LLM on past records, has a person annotate a blind sample of disagreements and random records in about an hour, uses the annotations to add rules and choose per-label thresholds, and exports a configuration to run Jev in production, with optional checks for drift.
author: Explosion

link.title: How Popp is saving 76% in token costs with Ellf and Jev
link.description: Using this template, Popp made their NLP pipelines more accurate, faster and cheaper

name: llm-classifier-eval
title: Evaluating an LLM Classifier
description: Measure a classifier that's built on an LLM prompt against people, without changing it. An action reads its logged decisions, sampling by label, or runs it over a random sample of texts, and saves its answers as one more annotator; people label the same texts blind after a short pilot, the built-in review settles every disagreement, and the annotation dashboard shows how often it agrees with the settled labels and which labels it confuses.
author: Explosion

name: create-ner-data
title: NER Data from a Panel of Open-Weight LLMs
description: Annotate texts with named entities using a panel of open-weight LLMs on your own cluster's GPU, with no per-token API costs. Three models served by Ollama annotate every text, correction rules fix the errors they make systematically, a Dawid-Skene consensus learns how far to trust each model, and a short yes/no review of the entities it's least sure of corrects it into a silver-standard dataset, with an optional corrected evaluation set.
author: Explosion

name: ner-jackknifing
title: Finding NER Annotation Errors by Jackknifing
description: Find the errors in a large set of named entity annotations by checking every text against a model that never saw it. The annotations are split into folds, a model per fold trains on the others as parallel jobs and predicts the fold it didn't see, and a review shows only the texts where the prediction and the annotation disagree, round after round until the data is in good shape, before training the final model on the corrected annotations.
author: Explosion

name: knowledge-graph
title: Knowledge Graph from Documents
description: Turn your documents into a knowledge graph of entities and relations, and measure how accurate it is. Entity mentions, links to your own entity list, and relations are labelled as separate steps by rules, models, LLMs or annotators, and each step is scored against gold labels from held-out documents, as is the final graph. The graph runs in Neo4j on your cluster, and every edge points back to the passages it came from.
author: Explosion

name: helpdesk-routing
title: Helpdesk Routing with Jev
description: Find out whether Jev is good enough to route IT support tickets to the right technician by problem area. Settles the label scheme in a pilot with a Gemini second opinion, builds a human-labelled evaluation set with an agreement check and a blind slip check, scores Jev against a bar agreed in advance, and sets up daily routing with a monthly problem-area report.
author: Explosion

name: support-insights
title: Support Ticket Insights
description: Extract products, features, error codes, versions and integrations from customer support tickets and route each ticket to the right queue. An LLM drafts the entity annotations, people curate them, a pretrained pipeline suggests the generic entity types, and the passes are adjudicated into a gold set that trains a custom spaCy NER pipeline and a separate routing classifier.
author: Explosion

link.title: Support Ticket Insights: Custom NLP with Claude Code and agents
link.description: How to turn an LLM prototype into a fast, cheap and fully private NLP component

name: github-docs-issues
title: GitHub Docs Issue Classifier
description: Train a binary text classifier that predicts whether a GitHub issue is about documentation. Annotate a single label with accept or reject on the included GitHub issues or your own, then train a spaCy pipeline on the answers.
author: Explosion

name: food-ingredients-ner
title: Food Ingredient Extraction
description: Train a named entity recognizer that finds food ingredients in cooking comments from Reddit or your own texts. Highlight ingredients with match patterns as suggestions, train a quick first model on CPU and a more accurate transformer-based pipeline on GPU, and optionally correct the first model's suggestions in a second round and check the annotations in a dashboard.
author: Explosion
